ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER A

Letter A — Apple.

Big A, little a and a shiny red apple — the friendliest place to start the alphabet, because snack time has already done half of the teaching.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does A say?

“a — aaa, like the very start of apple”

The letter is named A, but in apple you hear its sound: aaa — the first sound out of your mouth. A is a vowel with more than one sound; this short a is the friendliest one to start with.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace A a together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase A

Start at 1 at the top, slide down the left side to the bottom. Lift. Start at 2 at the top, slide down the right side. Lift. Start at 3, pull straight across the middle.

Trace the lowercase a

Start at 1 at the top right, sweep round to the left and all the way round the bowl. Lift. Start at 2 on the right, pull straight down.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Apple taste test.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Cut three fruits into slices — an apple and two others.

  2. 02

    Say aaa each time your child tastes the apple: aaa, apple!

  3. 03

    Ask which of the three fruits starts with aaa, and let your child be the judge.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
